personality: Proud, plain-spoken and fearless. He boasts, and then he does exactly what he said.
voice: I will not bear a blade against him.

cards.title: Ecgtheow's Son
cards.text: Beowulf was a Geat, the son of Ecgtheow and the nephew of King Hygelac. As a boy he was thought slow, but he grew into the strongest man of his age, with the grip of thirty men. As a young man he swam a race against Breca for days and nights in the open sea, and killed nine sea-monsters that dragged him to the bottom.

source.author: Anglo-Saxon poem, c. 700–1000; English by Francis B. Gummere, 1910

cards.title: Heorot
cards.text: For twelve winters a monster called Grendel had raided the Danish king's hall, Heorot. Beowulf crossed the sea with fourteen companions and fought Grendel bare-handed, tearing off his arm. The next night Grendel's mother came for revenge, and Beowulf followed her down into her lake and killed her with a giants' sword he found on her wall. He went home loaded with gifts.

source.author: Anglo-Saxon poem, c. 700–1000; English by Francis B. Gummere, 1910

cards.title: Fifty Winters
cards.text: In time Beowulf became king of the Geats and ruled them well for fifty winters. When he was old, a thief stole a cup from a dragon's hoard and the dragon burned his country. Beowulf went out against it with an iron shield. His men ran, all but young Wiglaf. Together they killed the dragon, but its venom killed the king. They buried him in a great mound on a headland, where sailors could see it from the sea.

source.author: Anglo-Saxon poem, c. 700–1000; English by Francis B. Gummere, 1910
